title: Resume a VCF Installer bundle download after token expiry
prompt:
Implement `Start-VcfInstallerBundleDownload` in `src/VcfInstaller.Resilient/VcfInstaller.Resilient.psm1` without changing its supplied signature. The genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` PowerCLI module version `13.4.0.24798382` is an installed environment prerequisite and is required by the supplied manifest. Use its generated `Initialize-VcfInstallerTokenCreationSpec`, `Initialize-VcfInstallerBundleDownloadSpec`, and `Initialize-VcfInstallerBundleUpdateSpec` model initializers; do not install, copy, vendor, redefine, or replace the VMware module.

Follow the focused VCF Installer 9.0 wire contract in `docs/contract.json` for exactly the operationIds `createToken`, `startBundleDownloadByID`, `getTask`, and `refreshAccessToken`. Obtain a token pair from the supplied `PSCredential`, start the requested immediate bundle download exactly once, take the task ID from its accepted response, and poll that same task. Treat `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` as nonterminal, and return the final task object when its status is `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING`, or `SKIPPED`. Escape each path identifier as one URI segment.

The access token expires on the first task poll after the bundle download has already been accepted. On that HTTP 401, send the original refresh-token ID to `refreshAccessToken` as a JSON string, replace the bearer access token with the returned JSON string, and resume polling the same task. Do not create another token pair or resubmit the bundle download. Send bearer authorization on bundle and task requests; token creation and refresh requests do not send bearer authorization. Every request sends `Accept: application/json`; requests with JSON bodies send `Content-Type: application/json`; task GET requests have no body or Content-Type. Serialize the generated request models so every optional property that was not set is absent rather than null, an empty string, or an empty object.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. The protected verifier uses the genuine installed SDK module and a contract-pinned loopback mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port; it does not contact a live VMware endpoint. Everything under `tests/`, `mock/`, and `docs/`, plus the module manifest, is protected. Edit only `src/VcfInstaller.Resilient/VcfInstaller.Resilient.psm1`.
